title: fix(desktop): start the take when Screen records a single display
body:
## Summary

"Start recording" with **Screen** selected did nothing on a single-display machine: the app hid, came back, and no countdown or recording started. Frame worked.

## Root cause

On one display, Screen mode skips the overlay because there is nothing to pick (`wholeDisplay` in `src/main/screenshots/screenshot-capture.ts`, used by both the macOS and Windows providers). For the `record` intent it answered with the `select` action ("Use selection"), which only sets the recording target: `applyRecordTarget` stored the display as the source with `start: false`, the capture handler restored the window as for a cancel, and `prepareRegionCountdown` / `triggerStartRecording` were never called.

That behaviour dates from the first overlay task, when spec decision 8 said "Screen with one display sets the target at once". Task 5 changed "Start recording" to open the selector, so the record intent is now only ever opened to start a take — and the one-display shortcut kept the old meaning. With several displays the chooser's "Record this display" sends `record`, so only the common single-display case broke. The existing test pinned the old `start: false`.

## Fix

- `wholeDisplay` answers `record` (not `select`) for the record intent, so the take starts on that display through the same path as Frame: `selectArea` → whole-display countdown on the shade → `triggerStartRecording({ reveal: false })`.
- Spec Task 5 notes (decision 8) now state the single-display Screen behaviour.

## Verification

- Regression tests in `screenshot-capture.test.ts` for both `MacProvider` and `WindowsProvider`: Screen + record intent on one display returns `{ kind: "record", start: true }` without opening the overlay. Both fail with the fix reverted (`start: false`) and pass with it.
- `bun run check-types`, `bun run lint` (0 errors; the 17 warnings are pre-existing and none are in touched files), full `bun run test`: 280 files, 2554 tests passing.

## Not verified

- I did not run a real recording in the app. The worktree has no Infisical `.env`, and a real take needs macOS screen-recording permission and someone to watch the countdown. Please QA on a single display: Record page → Screen → Start recording should show the countdown on the display, then record; the file should play.
- The rest of the Screen path after the start (renderer recorder with `area: null` on a `screen:` source) is the same one a multi-display "Record this display" and the old full-screen recordings use; I traced it but did not exercise it end to end.
